components: On the same internal carrier, swapping supplied effective neutral-current weights between fixed laboratory electron helicities preserves a total width and an electron-only unpolarized pole asymmetry. Their sign difference is observable in polarized production with the stated calibration.
candidates.declared_status: Reanalysis of published polarized and unpolarized summaries and a conditional dictionary contrast, not a derivation of chirality, new couplings or a fit to event data.
missing_bridges: Supply the external particle and helicity mapping, spin-one resonance and factorization, radiation/acceptance treatment and polarization calibration without importing the desired sign.

"""What does a polarized Z-pole measurement add to an internal charge table? On the existing even 16-mask carrier the 3+2 dictionary supplies a lepton doublet and a conjugate charged singlet. It does NOT identify a laboratory electron, its helicity, its current strength, a Z pole or any particle mass. This probe changes only a supplied coupling-to-laboratory-helicity assignment. It does not change a mask, pairing, charge, trace, anomaly check or invisible current. It is not a second chiral gauge theory or a cross-adapter verdict: the existing invisible-width adapter explicitly excludes visible new physics. For real effective chiral couplings at one factorizing spin-1 resonance, negligible external masses and the standard angular law, write wL,R = gL,R². An unpolarized partial width fixes only their sum (up to a common factor). The electron-only unpolarized pole forward/backward asymmetry is 3*A_e²/4; polarized production gives A_e=(wL-wR)/(wL+wR). No equality of electron, muon and tau couplings is used. The helicity-independent final-state factor must cancel; additional exchanges, altered radiation, or helicity-dependent acceptance need their own forward model. The conventional pole asymmetries use real effective coupling parts, but full widths include imaginary parts. Arbitrary complex Wilson coefficients are NOT compared to these data. Primary sources (offline rounded published summaries; no event refit): * SLD, https://arxiv.org/html/hep-ex/0004026, Eqs. (1)-(4), Table 1, text following Eq. (4), footnote 23. Counts are selected hadrons plus a small tau fraction, not tagged invisible decays. The sign uses measured laser helicity, measured Compton asymmetry and the theoretical Compton sign. Absolute beam polarization matters. Absolute luminosity cancels under the symmetry conditions, relative luminosity does not. Eq. (3) corrects for background, luminosity, polarization, energy and efficiency asymmetries and possible positron polarization. Pole extraction also corrects photon exchange and gamma-Z interference, depending on the calibrated beam energy. * LEP collaborations/working groups, https://arxiv.org/html/hep-ex/0509008 Eq. (1.66), Table 2.13, nine-parameter electron row WITHOUT universality. This is a corrected s-channel pseudo-observable: photon exchange/radiation, gamma-Z interference, and the Bhabha t-channel and s/t interference matter. It overlaps the LEP lineshape data, not an independent second LEP width. Its central value is an explicitly supplied sign-blind calibration. * OPAL, https://arxiv.org/html/hep-ex/0103045, abstract and Sec. 8. Distinct detector/sample from SLD and a different method: forward/backward tau polarization, assuming V-A tau decay and correcting radiation/interference. Use its separately extracted electron value, not a universal-lepton fit. No combined significance, likelihood, exact exclusion or model preference. Run: python3 -B -m scripts.probe_polarized_z_electron (also with -O). """ from __future__ import annotations from dataclasses import dataclass from fractions import Fraction as F from math import sqrt from scripts.probe_chiral_carrier_holdout import EVEN, LABELS, block def need(ok: bool, why: str) -> None: if not ok: raise ArithmeticError(why) @dataclass(frozen=True) class Run: name: str left: int right: int raw: str raw_error: str polarization: str # fractions, not percent polarization_error: str eq3_relative_percent: str eq3_relative_percent_error: str energy_gev: str collision: tuple[str, str, str] # central, statistical, systematic pole: tuple[str, str, str] def raw_asymmetry(self) -> F: return F(self.left - self.right, self.left + self.right) def polarization_only(self) -> F: return self.raw_asymmetry() / F(self.polarization) RUNS = ( Run("1996", 29016, 22857, "0.11873", "0.00436", "0.7616", "0.0040", "+0.02", "0.05", "91.26", ("0.1559", "0.00572", "0.00084"), ("0.15929", "0.00573", "0.00101")), Run("1997-98", 183355, 148259, "0.10583", "0.00173", "0.7292", "0.0038", "+0.16", "0.07", "91.237", ("0.1454", "0.00237", "0.00077"), ("0.14906", "0.00237", "0.00096")), ) SLD_96_98_POLE = ("0.15056", "0.00239") SLD_ALL_POLE = ("0.15138", "0.00216") LEP_ELECTRON_FB = ("0.0145", "0.0025") OPAL_ELECTRON = ("0.1454", "0.0108", "0.0036") def replay_counts() -> F: for run in RUNS: a = run.raw_asymmetry() n = run.left + run.right se = sqrt((1 - a*a) / n) # conditional binomial counting error, not pole uncertainty need(round(a, 5) == F(run.raw) and f"{se:.5f}" == run.raw_error, f"{run.name}: counts do not reproduce published Eq. 2") print(f"{run.name}: NL={run.left}, NR={run.right}; raw A_m={a} = {float(a):.7f}" f" (counting error {se:.5f});

={run.polarization} +/- {run.polarization_error}.") print(f" A_m/

={float(run.polarization_only()):.7f} (polarization only);" f" published Eq. 3 relative correction {run.eq3_relative_percent}" f" +/- {run.eq3_relative_percent_error} percent.") print(f" Reported A_LR at {run.energy_gev} GeV: {' +/- '.join(run.collision)};" f" corrected pole: {' +/- '.join(run.pole)} (stat, syst).") left = sum(r.left for r in RUNS) right = sum(r.right for r in RUNS) pooled = F(left - right, left + right) need((left, right, pooled) == (212371, 171116, F(41255, 383487)), "pooled selected counts") print(f"1996-98 pooled raw={pooled} = {float(pooled):.7f}; not a pole estimate." f" Reported combined pole {' +/- '.join(SLD_96_98_POLE)}; full 1992-98" f" {' +/- '.join(SLD_ALL_POLE)} includes these same events. Not recombined.") return pooled def asymmetry(left: F, right: F) -> F: """Nonnegative rates in a *fixed laboratory basis*, not amplitude signs.""" if min(left, right) < 0 or left + right == 0: raise ValueError("normalized asymmetry needs nonnegative rates and positive total") return (left - right) / (left + right) def carrier_and_controls() -> None: # External dictionary. Nominate one component of L and the antiparticle of # e^c. Neither the choice of weak component nor lab helicity is inferred. doublet = tuple(m for m in EVEN if LABELS[block(m)] == "L") singlet = tuple(m for m in EVEN if LABELS[block(m)] == "e") need(doublet == (15, 23) and singlet == (24,), "same carrier / external 3+2 labels") electron_ports = (23, 24) # second refers to the charge conjugate of this mask # Squared real amplitudes 2 and 1 (arbitrary control, NOT a magnitude fit). weights = dict(zip(electron_ports, (F(4), F(1)), strict=True)) currents = [tuple(weights[m] for m in ports) for ports in (electron_ports, electron_ports[::-1])] need([sum(v) for v in currents] == [5, 5] and [asymmetry(*v) for v in currents] == [F(3, 5), F(-3, 5)], "exact mirror control") need(asymmetry(F(1), F(1)) == 0 and asymmetry(F(36), F(9)) == F(3, 5), "equal weights give zero; nonzero common amplitude scaling leaves A alone") # In an *ideal resolved-amplitude model*, a phase or common real # orthogonal rotation of unobserved final channels preserves both norms. # Rotating the physical incoming helicity axis is NOT this invariance. for im in (-1, 1): for overall in (-1, 1): left = ((F(overall), F(im*overall)), (F(0), F(0))) right = ((F(0), F(0)), (F(overall), F(0))) rates = [] for z, w in (left, right): a, b = F(3, 5), F(4, 5) rot = tuple(a*x - b*y for x, y in zip(z, w, strict=True)), tuple( b*x + a*y for x, y in zip(z, w, strict=True)) rates.append(sum(x*x for row in rot for x in row)) need(rates == [2, 1] and asymmetry(*rates) == F(1, 3), "ideal squared moduli: sign, conjugation and unresolved-channel rotation") try: asymmetry(F(0), F(0)) except ValueError: pass else: raise ArithmeticError("no Z signal must not be labeled a zero asymmetry") print("Carrier L={15,23}, e^c={24}; lab port and current assignments supplied." " Real-amplitude (2,1) versus (1,2): total 5, A=+3/5 versus -3/5." " Neither magnitude describes the observed result.") def calibrated_mirror() -> None: """Exact coefficients (a,b) stand for a + b*sqrt(r), r fixed by LEP, not SLD.""" fb, fb_error = map(F, LEP_ELECTRON_FB) radicand = F(4, 3) * fb need(radicand == F(29, 1500) and 0 < radicand < 1, "physical central-value branches") sld, sld_error = map(F, SLD_ALL_POLE) # Only classify the reported sign, not the degree of numerical agreement. observed_sign = 1 if sld - sld_error > 0 else -1 if sld + sld_error < 0 else 0 same_sign = [] for hand in (1, -1): # Unit total is merely a common normalization. Multiplication by an # independent positive width scale gives the same comparison. left, right = (F(1, 2), F(hand, 2)), (F(1, 2), F(-hand, 2)) total = tuple(x+y for x, y in zip(left, right, strict=True)) diff = tuple(x-y for x, y in zip(left, right, strict=True)) need(total == (1, 0) and diff == (0, hand), "width fixed, difference reversed") need(F(3, 4)*diff[1]**2*radicand == fb, "identical electron-only A_FB") if diff[1] == observed_sign: same_sign.append(hand) need(same_sign == [1], "signed SLD observation distinguishes the branches") print(f"LEP electron-only pole A_FB={' +/- '.join(LEP_ELECTRON_FB)};" f" central-value branches A_e=+/-sqrt({radicand}) = +/-{sqrt(radicand):.5f}.") lo, hi = (sqrt(F(4, 3)*x) for x in (fb-fb_error, fb+fb_error)) print(f"Mapping the printed central +/- quoted error endpoints gives |A_e|" f" {lo:.5f}..{hi:.5f}; not a likelihood or a confidence interval.") print(f"Only branch {same_sign[0]:+d} has the SLD sign; its calibrated magnitude" f" differs from the SLD central value by {float(sld)-sqrt(radicand):.5f}" " (SLD minus LEP-based branch, descriptive only).") print(f"OPAL tau method A_e=" f"{' +/- '.join(OPAL_ELECTRON)} (stat, syst), conditional on V-A tau decay." " No joint significance, phase determination, or primitive verdict.") def main() -> None: replay_counts() carrier_and_controls() calibrated_mirror() if __name__ == "__main__": main()
